findings.issue: part2.htn:15 `theSlipstream` is an imperative script of one-off helpers: makeTrap, coverAt, gatherIntoTrap, finishTrap. Its feasibility is hidden in `trapSite` and in the helper bodies. You cannot read the `if()` alone and tell when the strategy works. It is the rubric's own slop example, almost verbatim.
findings.fix: State in `if()` what makes it possible: `enemy(?e)`, `not(immune(?e, snared))`, a skill with `skillAppliesTag(?s, snared)`, a finishing skill, and distinct allies. Then `do()` the states to reach with generic verbs: `applyTag(snared, ?e)`, then `prepareToUseSkill(?a, ?s, ?e)` and `useSkillOnTarget(?a, ?s, ?e)`.

findings.issue: ruleset.htn:13 uses an invented ontology. `blast(?el, ?feat, dead)`, `reacts/3`, `regionHas`, `role(?e, enemy)` and `status(?e, dead)` are used here. The same file's comments use `primer`, and part2 adds `trapSite`, `primer/2`, `signature/2` and `strikeDead`. That is an effect/reaction engine where the game's words should be. `blast(..., dead)` also makes terrain grant `dead` directly.
findings.fix: Use the game's words: `enemy(?t)`, `terrain(?r, oil)`, `skillAppliesTag(?s, fire)`, `immune(?t, fire)`, `hasTag(?t, burning)`. Drop `blast`, `reacts` and `primer`. An enemy weakness is a fact about the enemy, not a reaction table.

findings.issue: part2.htn:31 `first(and(canAct(?a), signature(?a, shield)))` uses `and`, which is not a built-in. It is silently false. The `else, if(), do()` on line 33 then fires every time, so the cover step never appears in any plan. Even if `and` worked, `else` is not a cut. Any later failure would backtrack into the no-op and skip the shield commitment.
findings.fix: Write the conjunction directly: `first(ally(?a), hasSkill(?a, ?s), skillAppliesTag(?s, shielded))`. If cover is optional, use `try(...)`. If cover is required, drop the no-op `else`.

findings.issue: part2.htn:31 chooses a skill by name (`signature(?a, shield)`), and the whole ruleset is written around one level's layout: 'the oil the level laid down', sludge, and the shield carrier.
findings.fix: Choose skills by their properties (`skillAppliesTag(?s, ?tag)`). Keep the level's oil and sludge as terrain facts in the level file.

findings.issue: part2.htn:36 `gatherIntoTrap` duplicates `gatherOthers` (ruleset.htn:18) apart from the `expose` step. The ruleset also has helpers that only one strategy uses: makeTrap, coverAt, finishTrap and trapSite. None of them is a reusable verb whose methods are different ways to reach a state.
findings.fix: Make one reusable verb, `bringMobToLocation(?t, ?l)`. Put each way to snare or burn in the methods of `applyTag(?tag, ?t)`: an ally's skill, the terrain at a location, or a nearby mob.

findings.issue: ruleset.htn:15 `theBurn` never states in `if()` who can apply the element: `castElement(?el, ?r)` hides the actor. The `?new` from `reacts` is bound and never used. The actors are not listed or kept distinct, and `try(gatherOthers)` commits to an allOf that is all-or-nothing.
findings.fix: Put in `if()`: `ally(?a), hasSkill(?a, ?s), skillAppliesTag(?s, fire)`, with a distinct ally who brings the enemy in. Then `do(bringMobToLocation(?e, ?r), useSkillOnTarget(?a, ?s, ?e))`.

findings.issue: part2.htn:42-43 `finishTrap` passes the primer `?p` as the actor to `strikeDead` and `blastDeadAt`. That contradicts the comment 'Never the primer'. When the terrain already exists, `?p = none`, so `none` is passed as the actor.
findings.fix: Bind the finisher in the strategy's `if()` as `ally(?f)`, with `\==(?f, ?p)` when there is a primer. Pass `?f` to a generic verb.

findings.issue: Each file opens with a 5-9 line essay (ruleset.htn:1-9, part2.htn:1-10, part3.htn:1-5) that covers design rationale, persistence notes and role philosophy.
findings.fix: Keep one header line per file and one short line per method or case, e.g. `% Case 2: terrain not there yet - make it first.`

core_upper.summary: This is the deleted core the_burn/the_slipstream design: imperative helper chains driven by an invented reaction ontology (blast, reacts, primer, signature), with the feasibility hidden in one-off helpers. It also has a silently false `and(...)` that turns coverAt into a permanent no-op.

findings.issue: theSlipstream never defeats the enemy. applyTag(frozen) runs triggerSnareEnemies before the enemy is lured in, so the allOf finds no enemy, try() skips it, and the plan ends with the enemy standing unsnared on sludge. The plan counts as a success, but the goal state is never reached.
findings.fix: Bring the enemy in first, then applyTag(?freezer, frozen, ?oilRoom), so the snare lands on it. Better still, end every strategy with the state it achieves (for example snared(?enemy) or health(?enemy, dead)) and check that state in a final if().

findings.issue: defeatEnemy marks theSlipstream as `else`, so FindAllPlans never returns it when theBurn works. The goal should be a menu of strategies, not a fallback chain. The two methods also repeat the same if(health(?enemy, healthy)).
findings.fix: Make them two plain methods, defeatEnemy(?e) :- if(enemy(?e), health(?e, healthy)), do(theBurn(?e)). and the same with theSlipstream, so each working strategy gives its own plan.

findings.issue: The if() asks for a lurer who can apply `magnetized`, but do() never uses the magnetize skill. bringEnemyTo lures with aggro, which any ally can do. So the if() does not state what actually makes the strategy possible.
findings.fix: Either give bringEnemyTo one method per way to move an enemy (a skill with the pull tag: prepare it, then use it; else draw aggro and walk back), or drop the magnetized condition and require only ally(?lurer).

findings.issue: applyTagEffect/triggerBurnOil/triggerBurnEnemies/triggerFreezeOil/triggerSnareEnemies form a small effect engine: physics cascades written as methods, each used by exactly one tag. Because the reactions are wrapped in try(), a cast 'succeeds' whether or not anything happened.
findings.fix: Keep the reactions as data at the bottom (e.g. terrainReaction(oil, burning, killsOccupants)), and have the strategy's if() require the reaction it relies on. Then one generic operator applies the known result, and no try()-guarded cascade is needed.

findings.issue: opApplyCondition adds condition(?target, ?tag) without a guard. Burning or freezing the same room twice, or snaring an already-snared enemy, adds an existing fact, and that error aborts the whole search. opGetAggro (line 132) has the same problem: nothing releases aggro, so luring the same enemy twice adds hasAggro again.
findings.fix: Guard in the calling method with not(condition(?loc, ?tag)) / not(hasAggro(?a, ?e)), and call opReleaseAggro once the enemy arrives.

findings.issue: opFreezeOilIntoSludge hard-codes a single terrain interaction into an operator name. The file also mixes the domain with the level facts (swarmers, rooms, roomSW oil) and names level-specific things like frozenSludge.
findings.fix: Use a generic opSetTerrain(?loc, ?old, ?new) driven by reaction data. Split the file into a reusable domain and a level file that holds only facts plus goals().

findings.issue: The file carries dead vocabulary and dead code: size/2, location/1, agent/1, the unused skills shield/lightning, opWound/opKill/bloodied, and opRemoveCondition/opReleaseAggro are never used. The health ladder is the kind of stat bookkeeping the planner should not need.
findings.fix: Delete everything no method reaches. Keep health to alive/dead, or better, to a tag such as hasTag(?e, dead).

findings.issue: The header essay is out of date: it says 8 enemies (the level has 3) and that Plan B snares (it doesn't). Plan B lists the freeze before the lure, which is the order that causes the bug.
findings.fix: Replace it with a one-line header naming the level, and keep one short comment per strategy that states its condition.

combatlevel1_greasetrap.summary: The architecture is right: a goal with strategy methods, skills chosen by tag through canApplyTag, generic navigate/lure/applyTag verbs, and room-level planning. But the Slipstream plan never reaches its goal, the else hides it from the menu, the magnetize precondition doesn't match the aggro lure, and the tag reactions are a try()-wrapped effect engine.

findings.issue: The file is an effect engine: applyAbility, applyEffect and effectOn interpret declared effect(?ab, ?who, ?atom) data with about 25 atom clauses and 5 recipient kinds. It has no strategy whose if() says when a plan works. The planner has to search a physics simulator to find out what an ability does.
findings.fix: Delete the interpreter. Write verbs that name a state, such as applyTag(?tag, ?t), moveTo(?a, ?r) and openDoor(?d). Give each verb one method per way to achieve it, with the feasibility in if(), for example skillAppliesTag(?s, ?tag), not(immune(?t, ?tag)). The goal's strategies then call those verbs.

findings.issue: The design runs bottom up. It casts an ability, then works out what happens next: reactions, weaknesses, behaviours, onGrant chases and pursuers. grantTag goes to afterGrant, then provoke, behaveAll, unleash and applyAbility. Outcomes such as dead come out of cascades and are not chosen by a method.
findings.fix: Start from the need, e.g. defeat(?e) :- if(weakTo(?e, ?tag), ...), do(applyTag(?tag, ?e)). Only write the reactions that a strategy relies on, and state each one as a precondition in that strategy's if().

findings.issue: The file invents a large ontology: locus, matches, weakFor, weakReady, receptive, anchoredAgainst, regionAtom, moment, spill, purge, pullIn, hook, heldAgainst, spotted, forcedStep, gapTakes, dashLine, teleLine, blinkLine, drawnTo, trudge, soak, reshapes, zoneReaction, onGrant, behavior, aimAt. The rubric lists moment and reacts/3 as slop by name.
findings.fix: Use the game's own words: ally, enemy, at, linked, hasSkill, skillAppliesTag, immune, hasTag, terrain. Add a new predicate only when these cannot express the fact.

findings.issue: The header is a 112-line essay. It holds a spec of the effect language, the map model, the reaction semantics and engine caveats about else.
findings.fix: Replace it with one line that says what the file is. Keep one short line per method or case.

findings.issue: opReact, opProvoked, opExploit, opFall and opKnock have no effect. They are trace markers for the simulator, not game actions. opForcedMove, opDash and opTeleport are three copies of the same at() move.
findings.fix: Keep only the operators the game engine executes, e.g. opUseSkill(?a, ?s, ?t) and opMoveTo(?a, ?from, ?to), each with one clear effect. Remove the bookkeeping operators.

findings.issue: Routing is hand-rolled: an 8-step hop/walkable iterative-deepening search over a custom edge/3. It also defines its own linked/3, which sits alongside the built-in's linked/2. The code is slow, bloated, and runs again on every if() query.
findings.fix: Declare linked/2 facts, with open doors as linked, and navigate with pathNext(?here, ?to, ?next), as in language.md section 6. Handle blocked areas at room level in the strategy's if().

findings.issue: opLoseTrack deletes tag(?npc, taunted), but loseTrack only checks follows(?npc, ?src). A direct chase effect on an untaunted NPC reaches the del of a missing fact, and that error aborts the whole search. The other branch calls opRemove(taunted) without checking that the tag is present. opGrant, opRemove, opNavigate, telegraph, canReceive, receptive, gone and forbidden are not defined in this file, so any missing one fails silently.
findings.fix: Put every deleted fact in the calling method's if(), e.g. if(follows(?npc, ?src), tag(?npc, taunted)). Declare the dependencies, or keep the ruleset self-contained.

findings.issue: The file simulates tiles and knockback. Every push aim is a plan, and so is shove :- if(), do(), which knocks into nothing. The file also simulates pits filling, gaps bridging, plates, chasers dragged each step, and zones reshaping. This is the maybe-walk, try-every-aim search that multiplies plans, and it plans far below the level where the game needs decisions.
findings.fix: Plan at room level. When a strategy needs 'enemy in pit', write one method, e.g. knockInto(?e, ?f) :- if(at(?e, ?r), feature(?r, ?f, pit), not(immune(?e, forcedMove)), skillAppliesTag(?s, push)), do(useSkillOnTarget(...)). Leave the simulation to the engine.

ab_effects.summary: This is a generic ability-effect simulator with an invented ontology and a 112-line essay header. It has no strategies, and the author does not choose the plans. It is the exact shape the rubric calls slop.

findings.issue: part3.htn:39-57 and part4.htn:19 define much of the vocabulary the rubric lists as slop: `holder`, `primer`, `guarded`, `exposed`, `open`, `vulnerable`, `free`, and `signature/2` as a skill kind. part3.htn:8-18 also has level facts `reacts/3`, `blast/3`, `strike/2` and `mark/2`, plus `takeVantage` (part1:59). The code also uses `role(?e, enemy|player|companion)`, `connected`, `regionHas` and `status` instead of the game words `ally`, `enemy`, `linked`, `terrain` and `hasTag`.
findings.fix: Use the plain game words: `ally/1`, `enemy/1`, `at/2`, `linked/2`, `hasSkill/2`, `skillAppliesTag/2`, `immune/2`, `hasTag/2`. Drop `holder`, `primer`, `exposed`, `open` and `vulnerable`, and state those conditions directly in the strategy's `if()`.

findings.issue: part3.htn:93-106 is an effect engine. `blastEntities`, `settleTerrain` and `sufferTerrain` are `allOf` loops that simulate what a reaction and a terrain do to everyone present, through the generic `opStatus`. Casts rewrite `regionHas` by `reacts/3`. The planner is searching a physics simulator instead of choosing among strategies the author wrote.
findings.fix: Delete the reaction, blast and terrain machinery. Write one strategy per winning combination, such as `burnOnOil(?t) :- if(enemy(?t), terrain(?r, oil), at(?t, ?r), skillAppliesTag(?s, fire), ally(?a)), do(bringMobToLocation(?t, ?r), prepareToUseSkill(?a, ?s, ?r), useSkillOnTarget(?a, ?s, ?r))`, whose operators have one clear effect.

findings.issue: The file has no strategy whose `if()` says when it works. Feasibility is spread across nested helpers (`castElement` → `holder` → `castElementAs` → `takeVantage`/`payFor`/`blastEntities`/`settleTerrain`). The actor is picked deep inside with `first(...)`, and cooperation is enforced by passing a `?not`/`none` exclusion argument through two arities of every verb (part4:30-40, part3:71-72, 110-111).
findings.fix: Put the actors in the strategy's `if()` as `ally(?a1), ally(?a2), \==(?a1, ?a2)`, along with the skills by tag and the target's immunities. Then `do()` is `prepareToUseSkill`/`useSkillOnTarget` for each actor. Remove the `?not` arities and the `none` sentinel.

findings.issue: ruleset.htn:44-55 is the 1-hop/2-hop navigation ladder that language.md warns against: `navigate` fails for any target 3 or more regions away. It also uses `connected/2`, which the built-in `pathNext` does not read. `first(and(...))` appears throughout (part1:54,61; part2:41,48,56,64; part3:47,80,114,122), but `and` is not one of the built-ins language.md lists.
findings.fix: Use `navigate(?a,?to) :- if(at(?a,?to)), do().` and `navigate(?a,?to) :- else, if(at(?a,?h), pathNext(?h,?to,?n)), do(opMoveTo(?a,?h,?n), navigate(?a,?to)).` over `linked/2`. Write `first(g1, g2, ...)` instead of `first(and(...))`.

findings.issue: Several wrappers and one-off helpers are not reusable verbs. `prime/2` and `prime/3` (part4:25-26) only rename `castElement`/`castElementAs`. `primer` (part4:19) is never used. `castElementAs`, `blastEntities`, `settleTerrain` and `markElement` each serve one caller. `lure`, `push` and `taunt` repeat the same actor, skill and vantage scaffolding instead of being methods of one verb.
findings.fix: Have one verb per game need, with one method per way to achieve it. For example, `bringMobToLocation(?t, ?l)` gets methods for pull, push and taunt, each guarded in `if()` by `skillAppliesTag(?s, pull|push|dash)`. Delete `prime`, `primer` and `castElementAs`.

findings.issue: `opStatus(?a, ?e, ?status)` (part3:34) is not a game action. It is a generic 'set any status' used by the simulation loops. `opCastRegion` takes five arguments and rewrites terrain from the `reacts` table. Its `add(regionHas(?r, ?new))` is unguarded if the region already has `?new`, and language.md says that error aborts the whole search.
findings.fix: Keep only the operators the engine executes, such as `opUseSkill(?a, ?s, ?t)` with `add(hasTag(?t, ?tag))`, and guard them with `not(hasTag(?t, ?tag))` in the calling method. Remove `opStatus`.

findings.issue: Reusable components name level specifics: 'the Warden's shield commitment' (part2:12), 'Magnetize' (part2:4,53), 'a flare' (part3:13, part4:43), and 'GDD 2' (part4:8). `holdPosition` and `anchored` hard-code one character's mechanic, and `metal(?e)` is a special case baked into `lure` and `push`.
findings.fix: Select skills only by tag (`skillAppliesTag(?s, pull)`). Move character and material details into level facts, such as `immune(?e, push)` instead of `metal(?e)`. Drop the named characters and skills from comments.

findings.issue: The headers are essays full of design history and philosophy: ruleset.htn:1-21 (control, RL-delegation), part3.htn:1-21 (the 'three rules of the chemistry engine', which then lists seven), and part4.htn:1-14 (GDD 2, role rules).
findings.fix: Use a one-line file header, such as `% Moving enemies: pull, push, taunt.`, and one short line per method, such as `% Case 2: no free puller - release an anchored one first.`

core_primitives.summary: This is the deleted core tree the owner rated slop. It is an effect engine that simulates reactions, blasts and terrain, built on the invented ontology the rubric lists by name. Actor selection and cooperation are hidden in helpers instead of stated in any strategy's `if()`, and navigation is a 2-hop ladder that fails beyond two regions.

findings.issue: part4.htn: navigateTo is a hand-built 2-hop ladder (direct, then one intermediate), so any destination 3 or more rooms away has no plan. The same ladder appears in escortTo (part3.htn:32) and pushToTarget (part5.htn:32). The shared verb every challenge depends on cannot reach most of a map.
findings.fix: Keep two methods: the base case `if(at(?a, ?to)), do()`, then `else, if(at(?a, ?here), pathNext(?here, ?to, ?next)), do(opMoveTo(?a, ?here, ?next), navigateTo(?a, ?to))` over `linked/2`. Handle blocked rooms by leaving out their `linked` facts (or deleting them when blocked), not by chaining more hops.

findings.issue: part6.htn: gates never constrain navigateTo, which only checks `blocked/1`, while the gate is `gateBlocking/2`. So `navigateTo(agent, ?dest)` reaches the destination whether the gate is shut or not, and the switch-and-gate strategy is decoration, not a feasibility condition.
findings.fix: Model a closed gate as a missing `linked` edge. opActivateSwitch adds `linked(?a, ?b)` and `linked(?b, ?a)`. The strategy's `if()` states which switch controls which gate, then `do(navigateTo(?who, ?swLoc), opActivateSwitch(?switch), navigateTo(?who, ?dest))`.

findings.issue: ruleset.htn: reusable components hardcode the actor as the constant `agent`. The same happens in escort (part3.htn:28, 38, 40) and pushable (part5.htn:28, 41, 43). No challenge can be done by a chosen companion, and cooperation between actors cannot be expressed.
findings.fix: Bind the actor in `if()`: `ally(?a)` (with `\==` for pairs), then pass ?a to navigateTo and to the operators, as gh_skills does with prepareToUseSkill(?a, ...).

findings.issue: part2.htn: each file coins its own vocabulary for the same ideas: `needsEffect/hasEffect` (tags), `npcAt`/`objectAt` (both `at`), `connected` (`linked`), `blocker`, `zoneEntry`, `switchIdle/switchTriggered`, `gateBlocking/gateOpen`, `cleared`. Readers and levels must learn parallel ontologies.
findings.fix: Use the game words: `at(?thing, ?room)` for actors, NPCs and objects; `linked` for adjacency; `hasTag(?t, ?tag)` for effects; `enemy(?e)` for blockers. Drop `needsEffect` and derive the missing tags from the goal.

findings.issue: part2.htn: executeCombo is a 3-step / 2-step `else` ladder over a global `comboStep` index, and opApplyEffect applies a tag out of nowhere: no actor, no skill, no `skillAppliesTag`, no `immune` check. The `if()` does not say what makes the combo possible.
findings.fix: Write the combo as a strategy whose `if()` names the target, `not(immune(?t, ?tag))`, and the skills that apply each tag. Its `do()` is `applyTag(?tag1, ?t), applyTag(?tag2, ?t)`, where applyTag has one method per way to apply a tag (skill, location, mob), as in gh_tag_application.

findings.issue: part6.htn: opOpenGate is not a game action. It is the consequence of opActivateSwitch, split into a second operator that the method must remember to call. In escort (part3.htn:12), opEscort moves the NPC but not the escorting actor, so the escort's two-hop path makes the actor walk separately behind the NPC.
findings.fix: Fold the gate opening into opActivateSwitch's del/add. Make opEscort move both: `del(at(?a, ?from), at(?npc, ?from)), add(at(?a, ?to), at(?npc, ?to))`, and recurse with pathNext like navigateTo.

findings.issue: part5.htn: the Sokoban push works at tile level, and `connected(?pushFrom, ?objLoc)` with `?pushFrom \== ?target` does not mean 'behind the object': any neighbour qualifies. The planner is doing geometry it cannot express correctly.
findings.fix: Either add an `opposite(?from, ?obj, ?to)` fact given by the level and require it in `if()`, or raise the challenge to room level (`bringObjectTo(?obj, ?room)`) and leave pushing to the engine.

findings.issue: part5.htn: the opPush comment says 'the agent also moves to objLoc', but the operator does not move the agent. The TYP001 `signature` boilerplate in every file is noise for the reader.
findings.fix: Make the comment match the effect (or add the agent move to the operator). Keep one header line per file and one line per method.

challenges.summary: navigateTo is the one reusable verb, and each challenge is small, but it is 2-hop only, ignores gates, and hardcodes `agent`. Each file adds its own predicates for things the game already has words for (`at`, `linked`, `hasTag`), and several strategies are `else` ladders with no real feasibility in `if()`.

findings.issue: The level runs on an effect engine with its own made-up words: behavior/4, effect/3 with remove/grant/spill, reach, suspends, heavy, kind, receptive, weakness/4, onEnter, feature/3, provokes, flinch, lure. The Wraith's state machine is written as data for a simulator to interpret, not as game facts that a strategy tests.
findings.fix: Describe the world with plain facts: enemy(wraith), hasTag(wraith, stealthed), immune(wraith, stun), skillAppliesTag(?s, blind), and so on. State each trigger as the condition of the strategy that uses it, not as behavior/effect rows.

findings.issue: The level file defines the strategies and helpers itself (win, iceOver, spend, reveal, aimFor, stepOut, confirmTag), and they name level specifics. For example, iceOver hard-codes effect(soulfire, ...) at line 141.
findings.fix: Keep only facts and goals(...) in the level. Move reusable verbs (applyTag, bringMobToLocation, prepareToUseSkill) and a planToDefeat menu into components. Write them without naming soulfire or the wraith.

findings.issue: The if() conditions of the win strategies are empty or only test stealthed. Whether a strategy can work is hidden inside spend, reveal and iceOver, so the if() alone doesn't say when a strategy works.
findings.fix: Put the needs in each win method's if(): enemy(?t), the tag that triggers it, skillAppliesTag(?s1, blind), a skill that can move it, ally(?a1), ally(?a2), \==(?a1, ?a2). Then do() is applyTag(blind, ?t), bringMobToLocation(?t, well), and so on.

findings.issue: `and` is not a built-in and is not defined anywhere, so `first(and(canAct(?a), at(?a, ?r)))` is silently false. The second stepOut method never applies, and only the do-nothing method at line 171 runs. Everyone stays in the crypt and gets silenced.
findings.fix: Write `first(canAct(?a), at(?a, ?r))`: first() takes the conjunction directly. Also drop the unconditional no-op method, or guard it with `not(canAct(?a), at(?a, ?r))`.

findings.issue: iceOver, reveal, stepOut and spend are each used by exactly one win method. confirmTag and confirmOff are assertions after a cast (they check that the simulated effect happened), not verbs.
findings.fix: Replace them with generic verbs whose methods are the ways to achieve a state, e.g. applyTag(?tag, ?t) with a skill case and a location case. The strategy's if() then already guarantees the result, and the confirm* checks go away.

findings.issue: The second win method is a script: reveal, then stepOut, then spend, then neutralize. It lists actions to perform instead of states to reach, and its correctness depends on how the effect engine resolves flinch, soulfire and melting.
findings.fix: Write the states to reach: hasTag(?t, exhausted), then the Wraith in the well or wet. Each state is reached by a verb with one method per way to reach it.

findings.issue: The 58-line header is an essay. It narrates the state machine, the map, each method and the traps.
findings.fix: Cut it to one header line that says what the file is, plus one short line per method, e.g. `% Blind it to trigger its spell, then drop it into the well.`

findings.issue: The mana facts and the 'one cast' timing window are bookkeeping below the level the game makes decisions at. aimFor (line 165) also works out targeting rules that the engine should handle.
findings.fix: Drop mana. Let the strategy's if() choose skills by their tags, and leave aiming and timing to the game engine.

fsm_wraith.summary: This level is built on the deleted effect-engine core. It defines a made-up behavior/effect vocabulary and puts one-off strategy helpers in the level file, and whether a strategy can work is decided inside the simulator, not in if(). It also has a silent bug: `and` is not a built-in, so the method that moves the team out of the crypt never runs.

findings.issue: attackUnit reuses ?Type, which line 111 already bound to the target's type. So only a unit of the same type can capture: a pawn can take only pawns, and a king only the king. Pawns can never take the king, so attackKing never works for them.
findings.fix: Use a fresh variable for the attacker, e.g. unit(?Unit, ?AttackerType, ?Player).

findings.issue: `\\==` is written with two backslashes. That is the C++ string escape for the built-in `\==`. In a .htn file it becomes a different atom that is not a built-in, so it is silently false, and attackKingAttackers and attackUnit never find a plan. The same problem is on line 118.
findings.fix: Write \==(?UnitPlayer, ?Player) with a single backslash.

findings.issue: The plain-move fallback in doMoveOrCapture is an `else, if()` with no guard. If the capture branch fails later, the planner backtracks into the plain move, which then moves onto an occupied tile and leaves two units on one tile.
findings.fix: Guard the case with the negated condition: if(at(?Unit, ?Current), not(at(?Other, ?Destination))), and drop the else.

findings.issue: The constants are uppercase (King, Pawn, Player1, King1-1). language.md says to write constants in lowercase, because uppercase names are quoted in the output.
findings.fix: Use king, pawn, player1, king1-1 throughout.

findings.issue: The rules use the cut `!` (lines 44, 49, 207, 208). The cut is not in the language.md built-in list, so it depends on engine behaviour that has no documentation.
findings.fix: Make each clause exclusive instead: printEndRow(4) :- nl. and opponent(player1, player2). opponent(player2, player1).

findings.issue: The header says 'only one thing happens', but the first two doAI methods are plain alternatives, so both give plans. Only the last three are an else chain, so the comment does not match the menu.
findings.fix: Make the comment match the menu: attacks are alternatives, the other methods are fallbacks. Or mark attackKing `else` too if a strict priority is meant.

findings.issue: The starting positions (unit/at facts) sit in the same file as the domain, so the rules cannot be reused with another setup.
findings.fix: Move the tile, unit and at facts to a separate level file, and keep the methods, operators and axioms as the domain.

findings.issue: Nearly every line of each if() has a comment, which is more than one line per method.
findings.fix: Keep one line per method (e.g. '% Move the closest pawn one step toward our king') and cut the rest.

game.summary: The shape is right. doAI is a menu of strategies, and each if() states what makes a strategy possible: an enemy next to our king, the opponent's king, or a king with no pawns guarding it. Each do() uses the shared verbs attackUnit, moveClosestPawnNearKing and tryMove, in plain game words. The flaws are correctness slips: the shared ?Type in attackUnit, the doubled backslash in \\==, and an unguarded else fallback in doMoveOrCapture.

findings.issue: stunAndBurn calls applyIce/applyFireball, which are never defined. It also leaves ?a1/?a2 unbound, so the strategy can never produce a plan. Its if() only checks enemy(?t), so nothing says when stun-and-burn is possible.
findings.fix: Put the feasibility in if(): enemy(?t), skillAppliesTag(?stunSkill, stun), not(immune(?t, stun)), skillAppliesTag(?burnSkill, burn), not(immune(?t, burn)). Then use do(applyEffect(stun, ?t), applyEffect(burn, ?t), opInflictDamage(?t)).

findings.issue: wetAndElectrocute checks only enemy(?t). It finds plans against electricityElemental even though immune(electricityElemental, electrocute) holds, because no step checks immunity.
findings.fix: Add not(immune(?t, wet)) and not(immune(?t, electrocute)) to the strategy's if(), and have applyEffect check not(immune(?t, ?e)) as well.

findings.issue: opCastWet, opCastElectrocute and the location method's useLocationToApplyEffect (line 123) have no effect, so 'apply the effect' never makes the target wet or electrocuted. The strategies list actions instead of states to reach, and later steps can't see that a tag is there.
findings.fix: Use one operator, opUseSkillOnTarget(?a, ?s, ?t) :- del(), add(hasTag(?t, ?tag)). Guard it with not(hasTag(?t, ?tag)) in applyEffect's if(). Give the location method a matching opUseLocationToApplyTag that adds hasTag.

findings.issue: castSkill dispatches on specific skill names (wet, electrocute), with one operator per skill. The skill name also stands in for the tag (hasSkill(?a, ?e)). Adding a skill then means adding methods and operators.
findings.fix: Pick skills by their properties with skillAppliesTag(?s, ?tag) facts. Replace castSkill and its per-skill operators with one prepareToUseSkill(?a, ?s, ?t) plus one useSkillOnTarget(?a, ?s, ?t).

findings.issue: Dead code: castSpellToTarget, doCastSpellToTarget, doSetMana, hasMana/manaCost and the skill/1 facts are never reached. The mana code is stat arithmetic, and its operators are not named op....
findings.fix: Delete the mana block and the unused facts. If a resource limit matters, model it as a tag or a fact that if() can check, not as arithmetic.

findings.issue: Level facts (agents, allies, positions, skills, immunities) sit in the same file as the reusable verbs, with commented-out companions mixed in. gob is both an agent and an enemy, and static/1 (line 145) is never defined.
findings.fix: Split the file: move the world facts and a goals() line into the level, and keep only the verbs and operators in the components. Delete the commented-out facts, and define static/1 or drop the check.

findings.issue: The second goToSameLocation method doesn't exclude the case where both are already in the same place, so it duplicates the first method's plans with a no-op opMoveTo(?a, room, room). opStayInLocation and opTargetAlreadyAggroed are operators that do nothing. Movement also teleports without linked/pathNext.
findings.fix: Add \==(?aLoc, ?tLoc) to the second method and make the base case do(). Remove the no-op operators, and move with navigate(?a, ?loc) over linked/2 using pathNext.

findings.issue: The only comments are banner section titles, and 'Attacker damages target' is wrong (there is no attacker). No method has a comment saying which way it is, and stale commented code stays in (lines 104, 163).
findings.fix: Write one line per method, e.g. '% Case 2: the location applies the tag - lure the mob there.' Delete the commented-out code.

gamehack3.summary: The shape is right: a planToDamage menu, applyEffect with a skill method and a location method, and a reusable bringMobToLocation/aggro verb. But one strategy calls undefined tasks, and the strategies check no feasibility in if(). The effect operators change nothing, skills are dispatched by name, and dead mana arithmetic and level facts are mixed into the domain.

findings.issue: There is one hand-copied verb per tag: doWet, doElectrocute, doWet2, doElectrocute2 and skillApplyEffect. Each repeats the same two ways (cast a skill, or lure the target to a location), so every new tag needs another copy.
findings.fix: Write one verb, applyTag(?tag, ?t), with one method per way. Method 1 is if(ally(?a), skillAppliesTag(?s, ?tag)), do(prepareToUseSkill(?a, ?s, ?t), useSkillOnTarget(?a, ?s, ?t)). Method 2 is if(locationCanApplyTag(?l, ?tag)), do(bringMobToLocation(?t, ?l), useLocationToApplyTag(?l, ?tag, ?t)). Then delete doWet*, doElectrocute* and skillApplyEffect.

findings.issue: stunAndBurn picks skills by name (hasSkill(?a1, ice), fireball). It does not check that ?a1 and ?a2 are allies, and it never checks immunity. Its do() calls one-off operators (applyice, applyFireball).
findings.fix: Write stunAndBurn(?t) :- if(enemy(?t), skillAppliesTag(?s1, stun), not(immune(?t, stun)), skillAppliesTag(?s2, burn), not(immune(?t, burn)), ally(?a1), ally(?a2), \==(?a1, ?a2)), do(applyTag(stun, ?t), applyTag(burn, ?t)). Skills are chosen by the tags they apply, not by name.

findings.issue: The file is a scratchpad with four versions of one strategy. wetAndElectrocute2 is defined twice (lines 70 and 129), so it has two unrelated methods. wetAndElectrocute3 and wetAndElectrocute4 call doEffectTE, which is a Prolog rule with no if()/do(). It is not a task, so both strategies fail silently. canApply, canApply3, ifCanSkillApplyEffect, ifCanLocationApplyEffect (which uses the undefined static/1), test_wetAndElectrocute, castice, castWet and castSpellToTarget are never called.
findings.fix: Keep one wetAndElectrocute(?t) :- if(enemy(?t), not(immune(?t, wet)), not(immune(?t, electrocute))), do(applyTag(wet, ?t), applyTag(electrocute, ?t)). Delete the numbered variants, the doEffect* rules and every unused helper.

findings.issue: The skill operators (applyice, applyFireball, applyWet, applyElectrocute, casticeOperator, castWetOperator, doCastSpellToTarget) all have empty del()/add(). No tag is ever recorded, so later tasks cannot see that the target is wet. inflictDamage fakes the result, and it is unguarded: add(damaged(?t)) errors if the target is already damaged and aborts the whole search.
findings.fix: Name operators op... and give each its one effect: opUseSkillOnTarget(?a, ?s, ?t) :- del(), add(hasTag(?t, ?tag)). Guard it with not(hasTag(?t, ?tag)) in the calling method. Guard damage with not(damaged(?t)), or drop it and let the goal test the tags.

findings.issue: The first takeAggro method adds aggro(?a, ?t) unguarded, which errors if the target already has that aggro. The second method only removes the old aggro and never takes the new one, so as a plan it fails at its goal. Note also that the arguments are called as takeAggro(?t, ?a), mob first, which is the reverse of the parameter names.
findings.fix: Case 1 is if(not(aggro(?mob, ?any))), do(opTakeAggro(?mob, ?ally)). Case 2 is if(aggro(?mob, ?old), \==(?old, ?ally)), do(opSwapAggro(?mob, ?old, ?ally)). Case 3 is if(aggro(?mob, ?ally)), do().

findings.issue: The feasibility in if() does not match what do() does. ifCanApply uses a cut and binds no actor. doWet then searches again for its own ally and skill, and its skill branch never re-checks immunity. The location branch teleports allies with moveTo(?a, ?aOld, ?tOld), and there is no linked/2 or navigation.
findings.fix: Bind the actor, skill and location in the strategy's or verb's if() and pass them into do(). Move with a generic navigate(?who, ?to) built on pathNext over linked/2, not a one-hop moveTo.

findings.issue: castSpellToTarget does mana bookkeeping (hasMana, manaCost, is/-, doSetMana). This is stat arithmetic below the level where the game makes decisions, and nothing calls it.
findings.fix: Remove the mana facts and castSpellToTarget. Gate skills with hasSkill/skillAppliesTag and tags. If a resource matters, model it as a tag or state, such as exhausted(?a).

findings.issue: The domain and the level are one file. Specific characters (companionE, gob, mimic), places (lake, inn) and commented-out roster lines sit alongside reusable methods, and the methods name the skills ice, fireball, wet and electrocute. Almost nothing is commented (R9).
findings.fix: Split the file into reusable components (skills verbs, tag application, strategies, planToDamage) and a level file of facts plus goals(planToDamage(gob)). Declare skillAppliesTag(electrocute, electrocute) and similar facts in the level. Add one comment line per method or case.

gamehack.summary: The skeleton is right: planToDamage is a menu of strategies, and a tag can be applied by a skill or by a location, which is the idea GameHack8 was later built on. But the file is an unfinished scratchpad. Verbs are copied once per tag, skills are chosen by name, the operators have no effects, there are four dead strategy versions, and aggro/damage adds are unguarded.

findings.issue: The strategies' if() only checks enemy(?t). stunAndBurn calls applyIce(?a1, ?t) and applyFireball(?a2, ?t) with ?a1 and ?a2 unbound. No ally has ice or fireball (those facts are commented out), yet the strategy still produces a plan. wetAndElectrocute hides what makes it possible inside doWet and doElectrocute.
findings.fix: State what makes it possible in if(): stunAndBurn(?t) :- if(enemy(?t), not(immune(?t, stun)), not(immune(?t, burn)), skillAppliesTag(?s1, stun), skillAppliesTag(?s2, burn), ally(?a1), ally(?a2), \==(?a1, ?a2)), do(prepareToUseSkill(?a1, ?s1, ?t), prepareToUseSkill(?a2, ?s2, ?t), useSkillOnTarget(?a1, ?s1, ?t), useSkillOnTarget(?a2, ?s2, ?t)).

findings.issue: doElectrocute has an empty if() and an unbound ?a, so it always succeeds. It plans electrocute on electricityElemental, which is immune(electricityElemental, electrocute), and the plan has no caster.
findings.fix: Delete this method. Route the tag through applyTag(electrocute, ?t), whose if() requires not(immune(?t, electrocute)) and binds an ally whose skill has the tag.

findings.issue: Each skill has its own verbs: doWet, doElectrocute, doWet2, doElectrocute2, applySkill(?a, ?t, wet), skillApplyEffect with =(?s, wet), castice and castWet. The 'lure it to a location' recipe is copied five times (lines 72, 79, 144, 169, 175).
findings.fix: Write one verb, applyTag(?tag, ?t), with one method per way to achieve it: an ally's skill (skillAppliesTag(?s, ?tag)), a location (locationProperty(?l, ?tag) with bringMobToLocation) or a mob's skill. Every strategy calls applyTag(wet, ?t), applyTag(electrocute, ?t) and so on.

findings.issue: The file is bloated with dead code and variants that are never called: ifCanApply, ifCanSkillApplyEffect, ifCanLocationApplyEffect, canApply, canApply2, canApply3, test_wetAndElectrocute, wetAndElectrocute2 (defined twice, at 120 and 155), wetAndElectrocute3 and 4, castice, castWet and castSpellToTarget. The ifCan* rules use the SWI cut `!`, which is not a built-in, and doEffectTE (line 140) is a Prolog rule that calls methods, so wetAndElectrocute3 and 4 can never plan.
findings.fix: Delete every variant. Keep one planToDamage menu, one feasibility rule per concept if it is needed, and applyTag as the only way to apply a tag.

findings.issue: takeAggro's first method adds aggro(?a, ?t) without a guard; if the target already has aggro(?a, ?t), the add aborts the whole search. The second method removes the old aggro and never adds the new one. Both methods are plain alternatives, so the planner returns duplicate or wrong plans.
findings.fix: Write two exclusive cases: takeAggro(?m, ?a) :- if(not(aggro(?m, ?x))), do(opAggro(?m, ?a)). and takeAggro(?m, ?a) :- if(aggro(?m, ?old), \==(?old, ?a)), do(opSwitchAggro(?m, ?old, ?a)). opSwitchAggro deletes the old fact and adds the new one.

findings.issue: The cast operators (applyWet, applyElectrocute, applyIce and the others) do not change the state. No hasTag fact is ever added, so 'wet then electrocute' has no causal link. Separately, moveTo, aggroMoveTo and goToSameLocation teleport between any two rooms and ignore linked/2.
findings.fix: Add one operator, opUseSkillOnTarget(?a, ?s, ?t), whose effect is add(hasTag(?t, ?tag)), guarded by not(hasTag(?t, ?tag)) in the calling method. Replace the teleports with a navigate(?who, ?to) verb that uses pathNext over linked facts.

findings.issue: A skill is named after its effect (hasSkill(companionW, wet)), and methods pick skills by name. Skills have no properties such as skillAppliesTag, and the level's facts sit in the same file as the domain.
findings.fix: Give each skill a name and a property, for example hasSkill(companionW, splash) with skillAppliesTag(splash, wet). Choose skills in if() by that property. Move lines 1-48 into a level file.

findings.issue: castSpellToTarget and doSetMana do mana arithmetic, which is stat bookkeeping below the level this game plans at. doCastSpellToTarget also has two overlapping operator clauses, and doStayInLocation is an operator that does nothing.
findings.fix: Delete the mana facts and castSpellToTarget. For 'already at the target', use a method with an empty do() instead of a no-op operator. Prefix the remaining operators with op.

gamehack2.summary: The planToDamage menu and the idea of two ways to apply each effect are the right start. The rest is a scratch file: verbs per skill name, a copied lure recipe, unbound actors, and strategies that ignore immunity. It also carries an unguarded aggro add and a large amount of dead or broken code.

findings.issue: The strategies `if()` only checks `enemy(?t)`. Neither strategy says what makes it possible: no `not(immune(?t, ...))` and no check that a skill, location or mob produces each tag. As a result, wetAndElectrocute(electricityElemental) still plans an electrocute that the target is immune to.
findings.fix: State feasibility in `if()`: `wetAndElectrocute(?t) :- if(enemy(?t), not(immune(?t, wet)), not(immune(?t, electrocute))), do(applyTag(wet, ?t), applyTag(electrocute, ?t)).` Do the same for stunAndBurn with ice and fire.

findings.issue: `useLocationToApplyTag` and `useMobToApplyTag` (line 156) have empty `do()`. Two of the three ways in `applyTagNotPresent` succeed without ever adding `hasTag`. Luring gob to the lake counts as 'wet', and bringing a mob to teslaTower counts as 'electrocuted', but the tag never changes in the state.
findings.fix: End each way with a game action that has the effect, e.g. `useLocationToApplyTag(?l, ?tag, ?t) :- if(at(?t, ?l), not(hasTag(?t, ?tag))), do(opApplyTag(?tag, ?t)).`, and the same for the mob case, with the mob and target in the same location.

findings.issue: `opApplyTag` does an unguarded `add(hasTag(?t, ?tag))`. `applySkillTags_L_ApplyTag` (line 126) uses `anyOf` to apply every tag of the skill (waterSkill gives wet AND clean) and does not check whether the tag is already there. A second water cast, or a target that is already clean, adds an existing fact, and that aborts the whole search.
findings.fix: Guard the anyOf method: `if(skillAppliesTag(?s, ?tag), not(hasTag(?t, ?tag)))`. Drop the second method: anyOf with no solution is the only case it covers, so give it an explicit `not(skillAppliesTag(?s, ?x))` base case.

findings.issue: `useSkillOnTarget` has an empty `if()`. It never checks that the actor has the skill or is in the same place as the target. The guarded version, `useSkillOnTargetSafe` (line 109), is dead code and calls the undefined `applySpellToTarget`.
findings.fix: Keep one `useSkillOnTarget(?a, ?s, ?t) :- if(hasSkill(?a, ?s), at(?a, ?l), at(?t, ?l)), do(...)`, and delete the `*Safe` variants.

findings.issue: The skill route only works if an ally already holds the skill. `canGetSkillAtLocation` (line 58) is declared but never used, so there is no 'go learn it first' case.
findings.fix: Split it into `prepareToUseSkill(?a, ?s, ?t)`: one method for 'already has the skill, go to the target', and one for 'go to the location from canGetSkillAtLocation, learn the skill (opLearnSkill), then go to the target'.

findings.issue: Names are noise. `applySkillTags_L_ApplyTag` is an invented, unreadable name. In `moveAndUseSkillOnTarget(?a, ?tag, ?t)` (line 101), the parameter named `?tag` actually receives a skill. `stunAndBurn` applies `ice`, not stun.
findings.fix: Rename to game words: `applySkillTags(?s, ?t)`, `moveAndUseSkillOnTarget(?a, ?s, ?t)`, and either `freezeAndBurn` or use a `stun` tag.

findings.issue: No-op bookkeeping operators (`opTagAlreadyOnTarget`, `opStayInLocation`, `opTargetAlreadyAggroed`) fill plans with steps that are not game actions and do nothing for the renderer. `opAggroMoveTo` (line 172) repeats `opMoveTo`.
findings.fix: Make the 'already true' cases `if(hasTag(?t, ?tag)), do()`, and delete these operators. Keep `opAggroMoveTo` only if the engine animates it differently.

findings.issue: The level facts (companions, rooms, gob, teslaTower) share a file with the reusable verbs. Commented-out companions and dead blocks are left in. There is no header and no one-line comment per method or case.
findings.fix: Move the world facts into a level file. Delete the commented-out and unused code (moveAndUseSkillOnTargetSafe, the empty trailing section). Add one-line comments such as `% Case 2: lure the target to a location that applies the tag.`

gamehack5onlyplans.summary: The architecture is right: planToDamage is a menu, and applyTag is a reusable verb with three ways to achieve it. But the strategies check no feasibility (immunity) in `if()`, two of the three ways are empty stubs that never apply the tag, and an unguarded add can abort the search, so this is an unfinished draft.

findings.issue: Each strategy checks only enemy(?t) in if(). What makes it work is hidden in the applyTag branches. immune(electricityElemental, electrocute) is declared but never checked, so wetAndElectrocute(electricityElemental) can still produce a plan. stunAndBurn applies ice and fire, not stun, and no ally has an ice skill.
findings.fix: Put the feasibility in if(): wetAndElectrocute(?t) :- if(enemy(?t), not(immune(?t, wet)), not(immune(?t, electrocute))), do(applyTag(wet, ?t), applyTag(electrocute, ?t), opInflictDamage(?t)). Make stunAndBurn match its name (tags stun and fire), or rename it.

findings.issue: opApplyTag adds hasTag with no guard. The anyOf in applySkillTags_L_ApplyTag applies every tag the skill has: waterSkill gives both wet and clean. If the target already has clean, add(hasTag(?t, clean)) is an error, and an error aborts the whole search.
findings.fix: Guard the tag inside the anyOf: if(skillAppliesTag(?s, ?tag), not(hasTag(?t, ?tag))). Also drop the second applySkillTags method, whose not(skillAppliesTag(?s, ?tag)) leaves ?tag unbound.

findings.issue: Mana is stat arithmetic (hasMana, manaCost, is/>=, opSetMana), and so is effort (allyEffort, moveEffort, increaseEffort, opUpdateEffort at line 195). This is TrunkThumper-style bookkeeping, and it is not the level this game decides at.
findings.fix: Delete hasMana, manaCost, allyEffort, moveEffort and the effort tasks. useSkillOnTarget(?a, ?s, ?t) becomes a single game action, opUseSkill(?a, ?s, ?t), plus tag application. Model limits as tags, such as hasTag(?a, exhausted), if the game needs them.

findings.issue: useLocationToApplyTag and useMobToApplyTag (line 184) are empty stubs. So the location and mob branches of applyTagNotPresent never add hasTag, and the plan still ends in opInflictDamage. Two of the three ways to apply a tag are unfinished.
findings.fix: Make them game actions with one clear effect: useLocationToApplyTag(?l, ?tag, ?t) :- if(at(?t, ?l), not(hasTag(?t, ?tag))), do(opApplyTag(?tag, ?t)). Do the same for the mob skill (the mob uses ?s on ?t).

findings.issue: opTagAlreadyOnTarget, opStayInLocation (line 202) and opTargetAlreadyAggroed (line 232) are no-op operators. They put non-actions into the plan; the engine has nothing to execute for them.
findings.fix: Make the base cases empty: applyTag(?tag, ?t) :- if(hasTag(?t, ?tag)), do(). Do the same for goToSameLocation and aggroTarget, and delete the three no-op operators.

findings.issue: The file carries dead and duplicate variants. moveAndUseSkillOnTargetSafe and useSkillOnTargetSafe are unused; the latter calls an undefined applySpellToTarget and compares a tag to a skill with hasTag(?t, ?s). The distance/3 facts, and the ?aOldLocation binding in bringMobToLocation, are also unused. moveAndUseSkillOnTarget names its skill argument ?tag.
findings.fix: Delete the Safe variants and the distance facts. Keep one prepareToUseSkill(?a, ?s, ?t) verb, with one case for an ally who already has the skill and one for going to learn it, followed by useSkillOnTarget(?a, ?s, ?t), as gh_skills does.

findings.issue: applySkillTags_L_ApplyTag is a coined, encoded name, and '% Unsafe' at line 195 means nothing to a reader. Neither reads as a game word.
findings.fix: Rename it applySkillTags(?s, ?t). Replace '% Unsafe' with a one-line case comment, per R9.

findings.issue: The level facts, including commented-out companions and skills, share one file with the reusable verbs.
findings.fix: Split the file: the level file holds agent, ally, at, hasSkill and immune facts plus goals(planToDamage(...)). The verbs go to components with no named characters, and the dead commented facts are removed.

gamehack4.summary: The skeleton is right: a menu in planToDamage, needs-based strategies, and applyTag with three ways to apply a tag. But the strategies don't state their feasibility (immunity is ignored), two ways are empty stubs, and the file adds mana and effort arithmetic, no-op operators, dead code, and an unguarded add that can abort the search.

findings.issue: The 'ally applies skill' method never binds ?a in if(). prepareToUseSkill's first case binds ?a through hasSkill(?a, ?s), so any holder of the skill can be picked, including a non-ally such as teslaTower with lightningSkill. The rubric's version of this method has ally(?a) in if().
findings.fix: Write if(ally(?a), skillAppliesTag(?s, ?tag)) so the if() says who acts.

findings.issue: opApplyTag adds hasTag(?t, ?tag) without a guard. If the target already has the tag (for example fire, from a second fireball-type skill), the add is an error and aborts the whole search, not just this branch.
findings.fix: Guard it in the anyOf method: if(skillAppliesTag(?s, ?tag), not(hasTag(?t, ?tag))). Tags already present then add nothing.

findings.issue: not(immune(?t, ?slowSkill)) checks immunity against a skill name, but immune/2 is keyed by tag (immune(electricityElemental, electrocute)). The check is always true, so this feasibility condition does nothing.
findings.fix: Write not(immune(?t, slow)), keyed by the tag as in the rubric's stunAndSlowSkill.

findings.issue: useSkillOnTarget has an empty if(). It never checks that the actor has the skill and is at the target's location, so the verb's feasibility is only assumed. useSkillOnTargetSafe (155) was meant to check this, but it is unused, confuses skill with tag in hasTag(?t, ?s), and calls a task that does not exist (applySpellToTarget).
findings.fix: Merge them into one useSkillOnTarget whose if() is hasSkill(?a, ?s), at(?a, ?l), at(?t, ?l), and delete useSkillOnTargetSafe.

findings.issue: useLocationToApplyTag and useMobSkillToApplyTag (222) are empty stubs. The location and mob ways of applyTagNotPresent never add hasTag, so a wetAndElectrocute plan leaves the target without wet or electrocute, and the second applyTag cannot see the first.
findings.fix: Make each one end in the same tag-adding operator as the skill route, e.g. do(opApplyTag(?tag, ?t)), guarded by not(hasTag(?t, ?tag)).

findings.issue: Dead or broken helpers make the file harder to read: stunAndSlowSkillDebug (99) and bringMobToLocation/3 (253) are leftovers, and prepareToApplyTag (201) is unused and moves the actor (?a) to the location instead of the target.
findings.fix: Delete stunAndSlowSkillDebug, prepareToApplyTag, useSkillOnTargetSafe and bringMobToLocation/3. Keep one verb per way to reach a state.

findings.issue: opTagAlreadyOnTarget, opStayInLocation (242) and opTargetAlreadyAggroed (266) are no-op operators that are not game actions and do not help rendering the way opSynchronize does. They clutter every plan.
findings.fix: Give these base cases do() (e.g. applyTag(?tag, ?t) :- if(hasTag(?t, ?tag)), do().) and delete the three operators.

findings.issue: Level facts (agents, locations, skills, with commented-out variants) share one file with the reusable verbs and strategies. The domain cannot be reused across levels, and the vocabulary includes an unclear name, applySkillTags_L_ApplyTag (172), with no file header (R9).
findings.fix: Move the facts into a level file. Keep the domain in components (tags, skills, movement, aggro, strategies). Rename the anyOf verb to applySkillTags and add a one-line header.

gamehack8agentattop.summary: The architecture is right: planToDamage is a menu of strategies, each strategy's if() states when it is feasible, and applyTag, prepareToUseSkill and bringMobToLocation are reusable verbs whose methods are the different ways to do them. It is unfinished, though: an unbound actor, an unguarded add, a tag-vs-skill immunity check, empty stub verbs that never apply the tag, and dead helpers.

findings.issue: `useSkillOnTarget(?a, ?tag, ?t)` passes the tag where the skill belongs (lines 92 and 96). `applySkillTags_L_ApplyTag(electrocute, ?t)` then finds no `skillAppliesTag(electrocute, _)`, the anyOf method fails, and the do-nothing base case at line 137 succeeds. Every plan that uses an ally's skill moves the ally and never applies the tag.
findings.fix: Pass the skill that `if()` bound: `useSkillOnTarget(?a, ?s, ?t)`. Delete the `not(skillAppliesTag(...))` base case so that a skill with no tags fails instead of doing nothing.

findings.issue: The strategies' `if()` checks only `enemy(?t)`. There is no `not(immune(?t, ...))`, so `wetAndElectrocute(electricityElemental)` is planned even though the level makes it immune to electrocute. You can't tell from the `if()` when the strategy works.
findings.fix: State feasibility up front: `if(enemy(?t), not(immune(?t, wet)), not(immune(?t, electrocute))), do(applyTag(wet, ?t), applyTag(electrocute, ?t))`. Do the same for stunAndBurn.

findings.issue: `opApplyTag` adds `hasTag` without a guard. `applySkillTags_L_ApplyTag` is anyOf over every tag of the skill, so waterSkill adds `clean` too. If the target already has either tag, the `add` errors and aborts the whole search.
findings.fix: Guard in the anyOf method: `if(skillAppliesTag(?s, ?tag), not(hasTag(?t, ?tag)))`. Rename the method `applySkillTags(?s, ?t)`.

findings.issue: `useLocationToApplyTag` and `useMobSkillToApplyTag` are empty stubs with `do()`. The location and mob cases of `applyTagNotPresent` return plans that never add `hasTag`, so the lake 'wets' nothing.
findings.fix: Make each one end in the game action: `useLocationToApplyTag(?l, ?tag, ?t) :- if(at(?t, ?l), not(hasTag(?t, ?tag))), do(opApplyTag(?tag, ?t)).` For mobs, reuse `useSkillOnTarget(?m, ?s, ?t)` on the skill that `if()` bound.

findings.issue: `useSkillOnTarget` has an empty `if()`. Nothing checks that the user has the skill or shares a location with the target. That feasibility lives only in the dead `useSkillOnTargetSafe`, which calls an undefined `applySpellToTarget`.
findings.fix: Merge them into one verb: `useSkillOnTarget(?a, ?s, ?t) :- if(hasSkill(?a, ?s), at(?a, ?l), at(?t, ?l)), do(applySkillTags(?s, ?t)).` Delete the `Safe` variants.

findings.issue: `stunAndBurn` applies the tags `ice` and `fire`: the name says stun, but the vocabulary has no stun tag. No ally has, and no location grants, iceSkill or fireballSkill, so this menu entry can never plan.
findings.fix: Name the strategy after its tags (`freezeAndBurn`) and add a `not(immune(...))` for each. Or add the `canGetSkillAtLocation` facts that make it reachable.

findings.issue: Dead code and no-op noise: `moveAndUseSkillOnTarget` (empty), `moveAndUseSkillOnTargetSafe`, `useSkillOnTargetSafe`, and the unused `opTagAlreadyOnTarget`, `opStayInLocation` and `opTargetAlreadyAggroed`. None of these no-op operators helps rendering. They only pad plans.
findings.fix: Delete the unused methods. Make the already-satisfied cases `do()` (e.g. `applyTag(?tag, ?t) :- if(hasTag(?t, ?tag)), do().`) instead of emitting marker operators.

findings.issue: Level facts, which name specific characters, locations and skills and include commented-out alternates, share one file with the reusable verbs. The file also carries unused vars (`?aOldLocation`, line 207) and an empty trailing section header.
findings.fix: Split it into a level file (facts plus `goals(planToDamage(gob))`) and a component that holds only the verbs, with no named entities. Drop the commented-out facts, the unused bindings and the empty header.

gamehack6swapskills.summary: It has the right GameHack architecture: a strategy menu, an `applyTag` verb whose methods are the different ways to apply it, and chosen skills by tag. But the tag/skill argument mix-up plus stub operators mean almost no plan actually applies a tag. The strategies also skip immunity checks in `if()`, and the file has dead Safe variants and no-op operators.

findings.issue: The 'ally applies skill' way never binds or checks ?a, so prepareToUseSkill matches hasSkill(?a, ?s) for anyone. That includes the enemy teslaTower (hasSkill(teslaTower, lightningSkill)), which can then be planned as the caster whenever the target stands at the lake.
findings.fix: State the actor in if(): if(ally(?a), skillAppliesTag(?s, ?tag)), as in gh_tag_application.

findings.issue: not(immune(?t, ?slowSkill)) checks immunity against a skill name, but immune/2 holds tags. The slow-immunity condition is therefore always true, and the if() no longer says when the strategy works.
findings.fix: not(immune(?t, slow)).

findings.issue: opApplyTag adds hasTag(?t, ?tag) without a guard. stunAndSlowSkill never checks hasTag, and useSkillOnTarget adds every tag of the skill (waterSkill adds wet and clean). If the target already has a tag, the duplicate add aborts the whole search.
findings.fix: Apply each tag of the skill through applyTag(?tag, ?t), which already has the hasTag / not(hasTag) cases. Alternatively, guard the anyOf method with not(hasTag(?t, ?tag)).

findings.issue: useLocationToApplyTag and useMobSkillToApplyTag (217) are empty methods. They have no operator, so the location and mob ways of applying a tag never add hasTag and do not appear in the plan as a game action. At 217, the head's ?tag slot receives the skill ?s.
findings.fix: Make each call an operator with one effect, e.g. opUseLocationToApplyTag(?l, ?tag, ?t) :- del(), add(hasTag(?t, ?tag)), guarded by not(hasTag(?t, ?tag)). For the mob way, reuse useSkillOnTarget(?m, ?s, ?t).

findings.issue: useSkillOnTarget has an empty if(). Nothing requires the caster to have the skill or to share the target's location, so the verb's feasibility is only implied by whatever ran before it.
findings.fix: if(hasSkill(?a, ?s), at(?a, ?l), at(?t, ?l)), then fold the skill's tags onto the target.

findings.issue: The file carries dead code. stunAndSlowSkillDebug duplicates the strategy. useSkillOnTargetSafe (155) is never called, calls the undefined applySpellToTarget, and tests hasTag(?t, ?s) with a skill. bringMobToLocation/3 (248) is an unused stub.
findings.fix: Delete stunAndSlowSkillDebug, useSkillOnTargetSafe and bringMobToLocation/3.

findings.issue: applySkillTags_L_ApplyTag is a coded helper name, not a game verb. Its base case, not(skillAppliesTag(?s, ?tag)), uses a variable that is only meaningful unbound, so it reads as a second alternative rather than as 'the skill has no tags'.
findings.fix: Name it applySkillTags(?s, ?t) and write the base case as not(skillAppliesTag(?s, ?any)).

findings.issue: The '%Unsafe' comment doesn't say what is unsafe (the swap drops an arbitrary existing skill, one branch per skill held). The empty section header at 266 and the scattered blank blocks add noise.
findings.fix: Write one line per case, e.g. '% Case 1: Ally already has a skill - swap it for the new one.' Drop the empty header.

gamehack7combined.summary: It has the right GameHack shape: a menu goal, if()-stated strategies, and applyTag with one method per way. But the ally-cast way can pick an enemy caster, the slow-immunity check tests a skill name, tag adds are unguarded, two of the three tag-application ways are empty stubs, and debug and unused methods are left in.

findings.issue: No component uses `agent/1` (gh_movement, gh_skills, gh_aggro, gh_tags and the goal all use `ally`, `enemy` and `at`). It is also incomplete: it lists gob but leaves out mimic, electricityElemental and teslaTower. So it adds a word to the vocabulary and states a world that contradicts `enemy/1`.
findings.fix: Delete lines 37-41. `ally/1` and `enemy/1` already say who is in the world.

findings.issue: No component reads `location/1`. Every place already appears in an `at/2` or `locationCanApplyTag/2` fact, so these six facts are dead state.
findings.fix: Delete lines 60-66. If sea must exist as a place, `locationCanApplyTag(sea, wet)` already declares it.

findings.issue: The `type/2` block is linter bookkeeping in the world file, and it has drifted from the world: ice, fire, stun and slow are declared as tags, but no skill or location produces them. About 30 lines of scaffolding hide the 20 lines of actual level facts.
findings.fix: Let TYP001 infer types from the component `signature/2` declarations, or keep only the tags this level can produce (wet, electrocute, clean). Put any type facts after the world facts, not before.

findings.issue: The level has three enemies that are never goals (mimic, the electricityElemental that is immune to electrocute, the static teslaTower). Nothing states whether they are meant as distractors or as tools. teslaTower at the lake is in fact a second electrocute source (gh_tag_application path 3) and a wet source, but the header doesn't say that this is the level's point.
findings.fix: Either state the intent as data (`funIntended`/`funExpect` facts, e.g. a solution through the tower and the lake) or remove the enemies that only add noise, such as the mimic in the start room.

findings.issue: "GH4-style world state" doesn't say what the level is. Line 3's claim that only wetAndElectrocute is viable is true today (no skill applies stun), but nothing in the file checks it, so it will go stale when the world changes.
findings.fix: One-line header: `% GH4: damage the gob; no stun source, so only wet+electrocute works (companions, lake, or tesla tower)`. Keep the claim as `funForbidden`/`funExpect` facts so `verify` checks it.

gamehack_gh4.summary: This is a correct, facts-only level file in plain game words (`ally`, `enemy`, `at`, `hasSkill`, `skillAppliesTag`, `immune`, `static`) with a single goal, as R8 asks. Its rough edges are dead or inconsistent scaffolding (`agent/1`, `location/1`, the `type/2` block), unused enemies with no stated purpose, and a vague header.

findings.issue: The `type/2` block (lines 6-23) adds a second vocabulary only to satisfy a linter. No component reads `type/2`, and it repeats facts that `ally`, `enemy`, `at` and `hasSkill` already state.
findings.fix: Delete the `type(...)` block. If the linter needs the types, have it infer them from the game words (`ally`/`enemy` give characters, `at` gives rooms, `skillAppliesTag` gives skills and tags).

findings.issue: `agent/1` (lines 26-27) and `location/1` (line 33) are coined predicates that no gamehack component queries. They are dead facts the reader still has to learn.
findings.fix: Remove `agent(...)` and `location(room)`. `ally/enemy` and `at/2` already say who exists and where.

findings.issue: The tags `ice` and `fire` are declared, but no skill applies them and no enemy is immune to them. The level has no use for them.
findings.fix: Drop `type(tag, ice)` and `type(tag, fire)`. Declare a tag only through a `skillAppliesTag` or `immune` fact that uses it.

findings.issue: The header narrates the planner's search path. Its claim that the planner 'backtracks to wetAndElectrocute' is also wrong: `planToDamage` is a menu of plain alternatives, and `stunAndSlowSkill` just yields no plan here.
findings.fix: Use one line: `% GameHack MVP: one ally beside the goblin, holding a wet skill and an electrocute skill.` Put the expected plans in the level's tests, not in the header.

findings.issue: The world supports exactly one strategy with one actor: the player already holds both skills in the goblin's room. The goal menu therefore returns a single forced plan, with no choice, no movement and no cooperation. The level only exercises the component; it does not play like a level.
findings.fix: Keep it as a smoke fixture, and label it as one. As a level, add a second ally, a `linked` room, or a `canGetSkillAtLocation` fact so that `prepareToUseSkill` case 2 or a second `planToDamage` strategy becomes possible.

gamehack_mvp.summary: It is correctly shaped as a level: plain game facts plus a goal, with no logic, and it uses skills by their properties through `skillAppliesTag`. But it carries a linter-only `type/2` ontology, dead `agent/location` facts and unused tags, and its world is so trivial that the goal menu has one forced plan.

findings.issue: The level uses two predicates for one idea. `skillHasTag(fireballSkill, slow)` says fireball slows, but `skillAppliesTag(fireballSkill, fire)` says it burns. `useSkillOnTarget` applies only `skillAppliesTag` tags, so the stunAndSlowSkill plan never puts `hasTag(gob, slow)` on the target. The strategy passes its `if()` check on a property the operators never produce.
findings.fix: Keep one game word. Replace line 84 with `skillAppliesTag(fireballSkill, slow).` (or give slow to its own skill), and change stunAndSlowSkill's `if()` to `skillAppliesTag(?slowSkill, slow)` so that `if()` and the effect agree.

findings.issue: Lines 5-38 are a second world written only for the linter. Every agent, location, tag and skill is declared twice or three times: `type(agent, player)`, `agent(player)` and `ally(player)`; `type(location, lake)` and `location(lake)`. Half the level file is bookkeeping, not world.
findings.fix: Delete the `type/2` block. Let the linter infer types from `ally/enemy/at/hasSkill/skillAppliesTag`, or keep the types once in a shared component rather than in each level.

findings.issue: `agent/1` and `location/1` are dead vocabulary: no component method queries them. They are also inconsistent: `agent(gob)` is declared but `agent(mimic)`, `agent(electricityElemental)` and `agent(teslaTower)` are not, while `type(agent, ...)` lists all four.
findings.fix: Remove lines 41-44 and 64-70. `ally/1`, `enemy/1` and `at/2` already say who and where everything is.

findings.issue: The skill names contradict their properties. `iceBlastSkill` applies `stun` but not `ice`, while `ice` is declared as a tag (line 29) that nothing produces. A reader expects the stunAndBurn strategy (ice then fire) to work here, and it silently can't.
findings.fix: Name skills by what they do (`skillAppliesTag(iceBlastSkill, ice)` plus `skillAppliesTag(iceBlastSkill, stun)`), or drop the unused `ice` and `clean` tags from the level.

findings.issue: The header claims both strategies are viable, but finding 1 shows the stun-and-slow plan never applies slow. Tooling comments (`for TYP001 linter`) are noise in a level file.
findings.fix: Write a one-line header that states the intended solutions truthfully, e.g. `% GH7: gob falls to stun+slow (two allies) or wet (lake) + electrocute (lure to teslaTower).`

findings.issue: The world has no `hasTag` facts, so in this level `opApplyTag` never re-adds an existing fact. The dependent stunAndSlowSkill method, however, calls `useSkillOnTarget` without checking `not(hasTag(?t, stun))`. A level variant that starts with stun on gob would abort the whole search with an add-of-existing-fact error.
findings.fix: In stun_and_slow_skill, reach the tags through `applyTag(stun, ?t)` / `applyTag(slow, ?t)` with the chosen ally, or add `not(hasTag(?t, stun))`, `not(hasTag(?t, slow))` to its `if()`.

gamehack_gh7.summary: The level has the right shape: facts plus one goal, in game words, with alternative strategies reachable through locations, learnable skills and a hostile tower. But half the file is duplicated type bookkeeping, and the separate `skillHasTag` predicate makes the stun-and-slow plan succeed without ever applying slow.

findings.issue: `skillHasTag(fireballSkill, slow)` is a second word for what `skillAppliesTag` already says. It exists only to satisfy `stunAndSlowSkill`'s `if()`, as the comment on line 101 admits. `useSkillOnTarget` applies tags only from `skillAppliesTag`, so the 'slow' plan never puts `hasTag(gob, slow)` on the target. The feasibility check and the effect disagree.
findings.fix: Write `skillAppliesTag(fireballSkill, slow).` and delete `skillHasTag`. Change `stun_and_slow_skill` to test `skillAppliesTag(?slowSkill, slow)`, so one predicate says what a skill does.

findings.issue: Lines 6-38 are a `type(agent|location|tag|skill, ...)` ontology that only the linter reads. It repeats the `agent/1` and `location/1` facts and the world's own facts. That is 30 lines of invented vocabulary in a level that should be only the world.
findings.fix: Delete the `type/2` block. Take kinds from the game words already present (`ally`, `enemy`, `at`, `hasSkill`, `skillAppliesTag`, `locationCanApplyTag`).

findings.issue: No component reads `agent/1` (lines 41-47) or `location/1` (lines 67-72). They are dead facts that the reader still has to learn.
findings.fix: Remove them. `ally`/`enemy` and `at`/`locationCanApplyTag`/`canGetSkillAtLocation` already name every character and place.

findings.issue: The level is built to maximize plan count ('all three strategies viable, all dispatcher paths exercised'), not to pose a decision. With four interchangeable allies and unordered `ally(?a1), ally(?a2)` pairs, most of the 'distinct' plans differ only in which companion walks where. It is a coverage fixture presented as a level.
findings.fix: State one hypothesis and give each strategy a distinct cost. For example, only one ally can reach the ice source, or the lake route needs the tower lured. Record the intent with `funIntended`/`funExpect` so `verify` checks it.

findings.issue: `skillAppliesTag(waterSkill, clean)` adds a `clean` tag (also declared on line 28) that no strategy or rule uses. Because `useSkillOnTarget` is an `anyOf` over every tag, each water cast silently adds `hasTag(gob, clean)`, which is state nothing reads.
findings.fix: Drop `clean`, or add the strategy that needs it.

findings.issue: The header and section comments describe test coverage and linter plumbing ('for TYP001 linter', 'dispatcher paths', 'unlocks stunAndSlowSkill precondition'), not the world.
findings.fix: Use one header line that says what the arena is. Where a section needs a comment, give it one short line about the game fact, not about which component it feeds.

findings.issue: `useSkillOnTarget` adds every tag of the skill through `opApplyTag` with no guard. This world starts with no `hasTag` facts, so it is safe now. But one level edit such as `hasTag(gob, clean)` makes a water cast `add` an existing fact, and that aborts the whole search.
findings.fix: Keep the level free of starting `hasTag` facts that overlap multi-tag skills, or guard `applySkillTags_L_ApplyTag` with `not(hasTag(?t, ?tag))` in `gh_tags`.

gamehack_multipath.summary: It is correctly a facts-plus-goal level on good GameHack components, but it is a plan-count coverage fixture with no designed decision. It carries an unused `type/agent/location` ontology, and the `skillHasTag` split means the 'slow' strategy never applies slow.

findings.issue: part5.htn: the anyOf branch of applySkillTags_L_ApplyTag calls opApplyTag for every tag the skill applies, and nothing checks for hasTag first. If the target already has one of those tags, add(hasTag(...)) adds a fact that already exists. That error aborts the whole search. It happens when a multi-tag skill hits a target that already has one of its tags. It also happens when a strategy calls useSkillOnTarget directly on an already-tagged target, because only applyTag checks for the tag.
findings.fix: Guard the branch: `anyOf, if(skillAppliesTag(?s, ?tag), not(hasTag(?t, ?tag)))`. Or route each tag through applyTag(?tag, ?t), which already handles 'already present'.

findings.issue: part5.htn: useSkillOnTarget(?a, ?s, ?t) never uses ?a. Its if() is empty. Nothing says the actor holds the skill, is at the target, or that the target is not immune. Callers have to guarantee all of that, so the verb's name overstates what it checks.
findings.fix: `useSkillOnTarget(?a, ?s, ?t) :- if(hasSkill(?a, ?s), at(?a, ?l), at(?t, ?l)), do(applySkillTags(?s, ?t)).` Leave the immune checks in the strategy's if(), as the rubric's R1 example does.

findings.issue: ruleset.htn:20, part3.htn:20, part5.htn:21: opTargetAlreadyAggroed, opStayInLocation and opTagAlreadyOnTarget are no-op operators that only mark a base case. They add plan steps that are not game actions and do not help the renderer, unlike opSynchronize.
findings.fix: Make each base case `do()`. For example: `goToLocation(?a, ?l) :- if(at(?a, ?l)), do().` Then delete the three no-op operators.

findings.issue: ruleset.htn: bringMobsTogether cases 2 and 3 do not exclude case 1. When the mobs already share a location, case 2 calls bringMobToLocation, which returns do() again. FindAllPlans then returns duplicate empty plans for the same situation.
findings.fix: Add `at(?m1, ?l1), at(?m2, ?l2), \==(?l1, ?l2)` to cases 2 and 3. Or make case 1 the plain base case and guard the others by negating it.

findings.issue: part2.htn: unlockDoor checks that there are plates and two distinct allies, but never moves the allies onto the plates. opSynchronizeOnPlates works from wherever they stand, so how the allies get to the plates is hidden inside the runtime operator.
findings.fix: Give plates a location in if() (`at(?p1, ?l1), at(?p2, ?l2)`). Then use generic verbs: `do(goToLocation(?a1, ?l1), goToLocation(?a2, ?l2), opSynchronize(?a1, ?a2), opUnlock(?d))`.

findings.issue: part5.htn: applySkillTags_L_ApplyTag is a coined name with an encoding suffix, not a game word. The signature/2 blocks in every file are linter metadata mixed into the domain, which adds vocabulary the planner never uses.
findings.fix: Rename it to applySkillTags(?s, ?t). Move the signature facts to a sidecar file the linter reads, or drop them.

findings.issue: part3.htn: goToLocation moves any agent straight to any location. It ignores linked/2 and does not check static(?a), although goToSameLocation checks static. A static mob can therefore be 'moved' by a direct goToLocation call, and room topology never limits a plan.
findings.fix: Add not(static(?a)) to the move case. If rooms matter, recurse with pathNext over linked/2 (the navigate pattern in language.md §6) instead of teleporting.

findings.issue: part2.htn lines 2-4 and 13-15 are runtime design notes (SynchroLens, 'pure marker operator', 'dispatched to'), not one-line statements of what each method or operator is for. part3.htn:36 and ruleset.htn:36 also keep unused variables (?aOldLocation).
findings.fix: Cut each header to one line ('Locked doors opened by two allies on two plates') and each operator comment to one line. Delete the unused at(?a, ?aOldLocation).

gh_primitives.summary: Right architecture: reusable verbs whose methods are the different ways to achieve them (prepareToUseSkill, applyTag, bringMobToLocation), with plain game vocabulary. Rough edges: an unguarded add in the tag operator can abort the whole search, useSkillOnTarget checks nothing, and no-op operators and overlapping cases produce clutter and duplicate plans.

findings.issue: The only task is `clearGreaseTrap`, and it calls `defeatGroup`, which no .htn file in the repo defines (it came from the deleted `components/core/`). The planner fails silently, so the level has no plan, and no strategy states in `if()` what makes it possible.
findings.fix: Write the strategies as methods. For example, `burn(?t) :- if(enemy(?t), at(?t, ?r), terrain(?r, oil), skillAppliesTag(?s, fire), ally(?a), not(immune(?t, fire))), do(bringMobToLocation(?t, ?r), prepareToUseSkill(?a, ?s, ?t), useSkillOnTarget(?a, ?s, ?t)).` Make the slipstream a second method built from the same verbs.

findings.issue: The goal is a fixed sequence that delegates to hidden machinery. It is not a menu with one method per strategy, so FindAllPlans cannot return one plan per way through.
findings.fix: Write `defeat(?t) :- if(enemy(?t)), do(burn(?t)).` and `defeat(?t) :- if(enemy(?t)), do(slipstream(?t)).`, then `clearGreaseTrap :- allOf, if(enemy(?t)), do(defeat(?t)).` or list the two enemies explicitly in the goal.

findings.issue: This is the invented chemistry ontology the rubric names as slop: `reacts/3`, `blast/3`, `hazard/2`, `strike/2` and `mark/2`. It is data for an effect engine, not game vocabulary.
findings.fix: Use terrain and tags: `terrain(corridor, oil)`, `skillAppliesTag(ignite, fire)`, `skillAppliesTag(freeze, frozen)`, and `immune/2`. Put each reaction that matters into the `if()` of the strategy that uses it, instead of into a table the planner simulates.

findings.issue: `role(?x, player)`, `role(?x, companion)` and `role(?x, enemy)` duplicate the plain words `ally` and `enemy` and single out the player. `signature/2` (lines 58-60) ties skills to named characters. Companions should be interchangeable and differ only in who controls them.
findings.fix: Replace these with `ally(player). ally(warden). ally(arcanist). enemy(swarm). enemy(bearer).` and delete `signature/2`. Ownership is `hasSkill/2`.

findings.issue: `skillElement/2` is a coined relation, and some of its values are not elements (`dash`, `pull`, `push`). `connected/2` (line 29), `regionHas/2` (line 40) and `lineOfSight/2` (line 35) are also coined. `pathNext` only reads `linked/2`, so navigation would never work with these facts.
findings.fix: Use `skillAppliesTag(gust, push)`, `skillAppliesTag(magnetize, pull)` and so on, plus `linked/2` for the map and `terrain(corridor, oil)`. Drop `lineOfSight` unless a strategy's `if()` needs it.

findings.issue: The `charge(player, ignite, i1)` tokens and the `unlimited/1` facts are resource bookkeeping. That is too fine-grained for a planner that decides at the level of rooms and tags.
